title: Case Notes — Returned Payments, Lease Late Fees and the Payment-Risk Share on Utility Pass-Through Service Late Fees
content:
**Rule.** For a late fee on a Utility Pass-Through Service statement, where a returned payment stands on the lease ledger or on the utility account in the last twelve months, the late fee is raised to 125 percent (a multiplier of 1.25); where neither carries a returned payment in the last twelve months but a lease late fee stands on the lease ledger in the last six months, it is raised to 110 percent (a multiplier of 1.1); otherwise no payment-risk share applies.

**Records read.** The lease ledger is the rent ledger of the Home-Site Lease the account serves; the utility account is the Utility Pass-Through Service account. A returned payment is a payment returned unpaid by the bank. An entry stands in the last twelve months when fewer than 12 whole months separate its date from the handling date, and in the last six months when fewer than 6 whole months do. The share multiplies the fee basis — the amount the statement's late fee is figured from — before the fee is rounded half up to the cent once.

## Cases (handling date 3 June, hypothetical)

| Case | Returned payment in the last 12 months | Lease late fee on the Home-Site Lease ledger | Share |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Returned rent payment on the lease ledger, 9 months ago | none | 125 percent |
| B | Returned utility payment, 2 months ago | one, 1 month ago | 125 percent |
| C | none on either | one, 5 months ago | 110 percent |
| D | none on either | one, posted 3 December (6 whole months) | none |
| E | none on either | none | none |

**Worked figure (case C, hypothetical fee basis 10.00).** 10.00 times 1.1 is 11.00.
